data.summary: The pod startup was delayed primarily by a cold image pull, which accounted for 79.457 seconds of the total 82.0-second startup time. The image size is 648 MB, and the pull throughput of 8.16 MB/s is within normal operating ranges, indicating that the image size is the bottleneck rather than network or registry performance.

findings.statement: The image pull phase lasted 79.457 seconds, representing approximately 97% of the total 82.0-second startup duration.
The image size is 647,991,705 bytes (approximately 648 MB), and the pull throughput was 8,155,250 bytes per second (8.16 MB/s), which is considered normal.

ruled_out.reason: The pull throughput of 8.16 MB/s is above the 5 MB/s threshold typically associated with registry or network performance issues.
The scheduling phase duration was 0.0 seconds, indicating no delay in pod placement.
Application initialisation took only 1.022 seconds, which is a negligible portion of the total startup time.

recommendations.rationale: The image is large, and moving to a slimmer base image or using multi-stage builds will permanently reduce the pull time.
Pre-pulling the image on nodes ahead of scale-up will hide the pull latency from the pod startup sequence.
